allowed_dependency_manifest.content: For each integer n greater than 1, consider the function E(n,x) = floor(n x) minus the sum from k = 1 to n of floor(k x) divided by k. Determine all real x that maximize E(n,x) among all real x, and determine the maximal value M(n) such that E(n,x) is less than or equal to M(n) for all real x, with equality for the maximizing x.

payload.statement_nl: For every real number x, x = floor(x) + frac(x), and 0 <= frac(x) < 1.

result_payload.proof_nl: Fix an arbitrary real number x, and let m = floor(x). By the defining property of the floor function, m <= x < m + 1. Define f = x - m. Then 0 <= f < 1, and x = m + f. Since frac(x) denotes the fractional part of x, we have frac(x) = x - floor(x) = f. Therefore x = floor(x) + frac(x), and 0 <= frac(x) < 1. This holds for every real x, so the lemma is proved.
result_payload.proof_summary: Use the floor inequality floor(x) <= x < floor(x)+1 and the standard definition frac(x)=x-floor(x).

used_external_facts: Standard defining property of the floor function
Standard definition of fractional part as x - floor(x)
